items.definition:
relating to or involving association
The associative property in mathematics states that the grouping of numbers does not affect the result.

relating to the ear or the sense of hearing
She has excellent aural comprehension skills.

of or like a tail; at or near the tail or posterior part of the body
The caudal fin of the fish helps it to propel through water.

Direct and outspoken; straightforward and honest.
She gave a forthright answer to the difficult question.

having the same relation, relative position, or structure
The wings of a bat and the arms of a human are homologous structures.

amazing, enormous
The view from the mountain top was stupendous.

relating to telepathy
Some people claim to have telepathic abilities.

not returned or reciprocated
He suffered from unrequited love for years.

Relating to or involving algorithms
The search engine uses complex algorithmic processes to rank results.

transmitted by blood
Healthcare workers must take precautions against bloodborne pathogens.

relating to the philosophy of René Descartes
Cartesian dualism is a key concept in philosophy.

relating to a dynasty
The dynastic struggles often led to civil wars.

relating to, caused by, or containing an enzyme or enzymes
The process involves a complex enzymatic reaction.

relating to the esophagus
The patient underwent surgery for an esophageal tumor.

able to produce or create
Artificial intelligence is making great strides in generative art.

not to be allowed or tolerated
The evidence was ruled inadmissible in court.

impossible to defeat or subdue
Her indomitable spirit helped her overcome many challenges.

relating to jurisdiction
There was a jurisdictional dispute between the two courts.

Extremely unpleasant; repulsive.
He had to perform the odious task of cleaning the toilets.

laying down rules or instructions
The grammar book takes a prescriptive approach to language rules.

crossing a continent
The transcontinental railroad connected the east and west coasts.

relating to typography or printing
The book contained several typographical errors.

honorable and respectable
He was known as an upstanding member of the community.

having a very eager approach to an activity; wanting or devouring great quantities of food.
He has a voracious appetite for books.

(of a bad act) done on purpose; (of a person) determined to do what they want.
Her willful disobedience led to consequences.

showing, feeling, or relating to sexual desire.
He made amorous advances towards her.

suffering from anemia; lacking in color, spirit, or vitality.
She felt weak and anemic after her illness.

covered or flooded
The deck was awash with seawater.

unpleasant or cruel
The weather was absolutely beastly today.

intended to placate or reconcile
He adopted a conciliatory tone to resolve the dispute.

already determined or inevitable
The outcome of the election was a foregone conclusion.

Intelligently analytical and clear-thinking
Her incisive comments cut to the heart of the matter.

Not welcoming or providing shelter
The desert is an inhospitable environment for most plants.

Not able to be operated on or used
The tumor was deemed inoperable by the surgeons.

marked with spots or smears of color
The old wall had a mottled appearance due to years of weathering.

unequaled; unrivaled
Her peerless talent for music was evident from a young age.

allowing liquids or gases to pass through it
The soil was highly permeable, allowing water to drain quickly.

avoiding the company of other people; solitary
The reclusive author rarely left his isolated cabin.

of various kinds; several
The shop sells sundry items for the home.

of a verb or a sense of a verb) able to take a direct object
The verb 'eat' can be transitive, as in 'I eat apples'.

not right or reasonable; shockingly unfair or unjust
The company's actions were deemed unconscionable by the court.

like a cavern in size, shape, or atmosphere
The old warehouse was cavernous and empty.

having or showing great knowledge or learning
The professor was known for his erudite lectures.

feeling or expressing pensive sadness
The melancholic music perfectly suited his mood.

vague; unclear
The plan remained nebulous, with no clear details.

occurring or born before the full term of gestation
The baby was born preterm, at 30 weeks.

relating to or resembling a prism; showing colors like a prism
The crystal refracted the light into a beautiful prismatic display.

tending to present a subject or problem in a simplified or oversimplified way
His argument was overly reductive, ignoring many complexities.

denoting a loan offered to a borrower with a poor credit rating
The subprime mortgage crisis had a significant impact on the economy.

relating to the Teutons or Germans
The architecture had a distinct Teutonic influence.

consisting of three parts
The agreement was tripartite, involving three different nations.

intended to teach, particularly in having moral instruction as an ulterior motive
The novel had a strong didactic purpose, aiming to educate readers about social issues.

Constituting or expressed as a conventional formula or set form.
His speeches often sound very formulaic and uninspired.

Causing horror or disgust.
The detective described the grisly scene of the crime.

Characterized by individualism; independent and self-reliant.
She has a very individualistic approach to fashion.

impossible to deny or disprove
The evidence presented was irrefutable.

relating to the economic theories of John Maynard Keynes
Keynesian economics influenced government policy for decades.

well-chosen or happening at a favorable time
He seized the opportune moment to ask for a raise.

expressing contempt or disapproval
The term "spinster" is often considered pejorative.

relating to projection or a project
Projective geometry is a branch of mathematics that studies properties of geometric figures that are invariant under projective transformations.

optimistic or positive, especially in an apparently difficult situation
He remained sanguine about the company's future despite the recent economic downturn.

born dead; failed to develop or come into existence
The project was stillborn due to lack of funding.

relating to a zone or zones
The climate exhibits distinct zonal variations.

suffering from anorexia
The doctor was concerned about the patient's anorexic tendencies.
